Map of Swiss Spatial Units

Source: R/map-tools.R
plotMap.Rd

Draws spatial units (municipalities, districts, cantons, regions) and colours a selection of them. This is the quick way to a choropleth map of municipal or cantonal statistics, and to highlight single units.

Usage

plotMap(
  map,
  id = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  col = NA,
  border = "grey",
  lwd = 1,
  bg = "white",
  labels = FALSE,
  vegetation = FALSE,
  add = FALSE,
  stamp = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

map

an sf object from geoGemeinde(), geoKanton(), geoThemakart() etc., or a unit name passed to geoThemakart(), e.g. "kanton".

id

ids of the units to colour, cantons also by abbreviation (e.g. "ZH"); NULL for all units.

main

plot title; NULL, "", NA or FALSE draw none.

col

fill colours, recycled along id.

border

border colours, recycled along id.

lwd

border line width.

bg

fill colour of the units not in id.

labels

TRUE to label the units in id with their ids, a character vector of labels along id, or a list holding such a value (unnamed or as text) and further arguments of text() (cex, col, font, adj, pos, offset); FALSE draws none.

vegetation

the vegetation area of ThemaKart maps: TRUE draws it with default colours, FALSE, NULL or NA draw none, a list list(col = , border = , lwd = ) sets its style.

add

logical; if TRUE, the map is added to the current plot.

stamp

source note of ThemaKart maps: TRUE draws it, FALSE, NULL or NA suppress it, a list passes arguments to stampBfs(). Ignored with add = TRUE and for maps of other sources.

...

further graphical parameters passed to plot() for the geometry.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame with the id and the label coordinates x, y of the units in id, for use with text().

Details

Units not listed in id are drawn with the fill colour bg and a grey border (unless add = TRUE). With a ThemaKart map the vegetation area can be overlaid and labels are placed at the official label points; otherwise at sf::st_point_on_surface(). ThemaKart maps get the mandatory source note (see stampBfs()).

See also

addGewaesser(), combineRegions().

Other swiss.map: addGewaesser(), stampBfs()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plotMap("kanton", id = c("ZH", "BE"), col = c("steelblue", "orange"),
        labels = TRUE)
addGewaesser()

# choropleth of the population by municipality
pop <- popGemeinde(2021)
geo <- geoGemeinde(unique(pop$gem_stand_d))   # stand of the population cube
pop <- aggregate(ch_n ~ gem_id, data = pop, FUN = sum)
br  <- cut(log10(pop$ch_n), 6)
plotMap(geo, id = pop$gem_id,
        col = hcl.colors(6, "Blues 3", rev = TRUE)[br], border = NA)
} # }
